headline: PALADIN PLS ATLAS HITS 4.25% URANIUM IN SALOON TREND — 8.0m At 1.75% U3O8 In New Zone Parallel To Triple R; 7 Of 8 Holes Mineralized At Saskatchewan PLS Project
snippet: Paladin Energy Ltd (TSX/ASX: PDN) announced September 2 that its Patterson Lake South Project's Atlas discovery has delivered its strongest results to date in the Saloon Trend of Saskatchewan: hole PLS26-708B returned 8.0 metres averaging 1.75% U3O8 including a 3.0-metre interval grading 4.25% U3O8 from 190 metres depth — comfortably high-grade by global uranium standards. Seven of eight drill holes intersected significant uranium mineralisation across 2,408 metres drilled, extending the Atlas zone parallel to and south of Triple R, confirming a new high-grade discovery corridor alongside the Saloon East discovery of 2025. eU3O8 values are preliminary pending chemical assay, but 4.25% intervals are consistent with Triple R's high-grade core intercepts that underpinned Fission Uranium's resource — now held by Paladin. A parallel high-grade discovery within a district already hosting one of the world's richest undeveloped uranium deposits expands PLS's resource potential substantially and reinforces the multi-deposit camp thesis that originally attracted Paladin to the acquisition.

headline: GREENLAND GOVT APPROVES SARFARTOQ — Greenland Mines Closes $2.05B NPV Nd-Pr Acquisition; Project Would Produce 34% Of All NdPr Refined Outside China
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd (NASDAQ: GRML) completed its acquisition of the Sarfartoq Nd-Pr Rare Earth Project in southwest Greenland on September 2 following formal approval from the Government of Greenland — a jurisdiction of growing strategic importance to Western rare earth supply chain policy. The project's published scoping study values Sarfartoq at up to US$2.05 billion pre-tax NPV with a 118.6% pre-tax IRR, and at planned annual neodymium-praseodymium oxide production rates across its nine scheduled operating years, the project would represent approximately 34% of all NdPr oxide refined outside China at 2025 consumption levels. Greenland Mines paid US$20 million cash plus US$15 million in securities for Neo North Star Resources to acquire the project. Greenland's legal framework gives the government a stake in large-scale extractive projects, making the approval a meaningful signal of sovereign alignment with Western magnet metals strategy. The company's technical team returns to site in September for infill drilling, pilot-scale metallurgical testing, and mine engineering planning ahead of pre-feasibility study.

headline: GOLD MINERS CAP BEST AUGUST SINCE 1994 — NYSE Arca Index +33%, 3X Gold's Move; GDX Logs $419M In Monthly Inflows As Debasement Trade Accelerates
snippet: The NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index climbed 33% in August 2026 — the best single-month performance since at least 1994, Bloomberg reported September 1. Gold mining equities outpaced bullion by more than three times: bullion gained approximately 10% in August while miners tripled that return as investors positioned for margin expansion at $4,400+ gold. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) logged its highest monthly inflows since February 2026 at $419 million, signalling institutional-scale conviction in the debasement trade — a thesis connecting persistent fiscal deficits, sovereign debt monetisation, and geopolitical instability to long-duration commodity-equity purchases. For junior mining investors, the August rotation into senior producers is a historically reliable leading indicator: institutional flows toward majors have typically been followed by retail and junior-focused capital within one to three months, making the current moment a potentially pivotal setup for undiscovered and undercovered junior names.

headline: ROXMORE DRILLS 94.5m AT 0.73 g/t Au AT NEVADA CONVERSE — Battle Mountain-Eureka Trend; 3 Rigs Running On 30,000m Program; Updated Resource + PFS Target 2027
snippet: Roxmore Resources (OTC: GARLF) released infill and extension drill results September 1 from the Converse Gold Project on Nevada's Battle Mountain-Eureka Gold Trend: step-out hole CV26-022 returned 94.5 metres grading 0.73 g/t gold and 2.34 g/t silver, while infill hole CV26-017 intersected 85.3 metres at 0.52 g/t Au. Additional intervals included 62.5 metres at 0.79 g/t Au and 3.16 g/t Ag with a 39.6-metre sub-interval at 1.07 g/t Au. Three drill rigs are now operating simultaneously — one RC and two diamond core — on a 30,000-metre Phase 1 program approximately 31% complete, building toward an updated NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate and a preliminary feasibility study targeted for 2027. Bulk-tonnage oxide gold on Nevada's premier gold trend, with three-rig drilling intensity and an accelerated development timeline, is the profile that historically attracts institutional coverage and mid-tier M&A interest at a tier-1, low-risk jurisdiction like Nevada.

headline: THISTLE RESOURCES STARTS PHASE 3 AT MIDDLE RIVER GOLD — 3,000m Drill Underway In Bathurst Camp NB; 50+ Priority Targets Along 7km Trend Ahead Of Resource Update
snippet: Thistle Resources Inc. (TSXV: TRCG) announced September 3 the start of its Phase 3 diamond drill program at the Middle River Gold Project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp — one of Canada's historically prolific multi-metal districts that includes the giant Brunswick No. 12 zinc-lead-silver mine. The 3,000-metre program continues systematic expansion of the MRG Upper Zone along a 7-kilometre gold-mineralised fold system identified using Abitibi Geophysics' 3D Orion Vision Technology, which has outlined more than 50 high-priority drill target centres across the trend. Results from Phase 3 drilling will support an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate, with Thistle targeting a resource definition objective of over 2,000,000 ounces of gold across the system. Previous drilling returned 1.65 g/t Au over 20.71 metres including 3.36 g/t Au over 7.82 metres in Hole 21TRC-AU007, and the Company is fully funded for the current phase with permits in hand across the trend.

headline: DYNASTY GOLD DRILLS FOR MET SAMPLES AT THUNDERCLOUD — Pelham Open-Pit Design Advances To Metallurgical Testing Phase In NW Ontario Greenstone Belt
snippet: Dynasty Gold Corp. (TSXV: DYG) announced September 3 the commencement of its metallurgical drilling program at the Thundercloud Property in the Manitou-Stormy Lakes greenstone belt of Northwestern Ontario — 200 kilometres southeast of the Red Lake gold mining hub and 47 kilometres southeast of Dryden. The program obtains representative core samples from the Pelham deposit in zones earmarked for an open-pit mining scenario, providing the raw material for metallurgical testwork that is a regulatory and technical prerequisite for any preliminary economic assessment or feasibility study. The September 2021 NI 43-101 resource estimate for Pelham underpins the planned surface-accessible open-pit study. For investors tracking development milestones, commencement of metallurgical testing is the technical step that converts a defined resource into a project with a known processing pathway — one of the clearest signals that a developer is actively progressing toward a production decision rather than simply accumulating drilling data.

headline: METAL ENERGY DOUBLES DRILL CAPACITY AT NIV COPPER-GOLD-MOLY — Second Rig Joins 5km Toodoggone BC Porphyry Test In Final Weeks Of 2026 Season
snippet: Metal Energy Corp. (TSXV: MERG) announced September 3 that a second diamond drill rig has been mobilised to the NIV copper-gold-molybdenum project in British Columbia's Toodoggone District — a porphyry-rich belt that hosts Kemess, Mount Milligan, and multiple other large deposits. Six holes totalling approximately 4,200 metres have been completed toward the 6,000-metre 2026 target, and the additional rig doubles drilling capacity for the final four weeks of the field season to complete a more thorough test of the 5-kilometre mineralised NIV system. The second rig will focus on the most encouraging holes drilled to date, targeting the structural corridors most likely to host economic copper-gold mineralisation. Assay results will be released on receipt; a comprehensive test of a 5-kilometre porphyry-scale strike in one of BC's premier exploration districts positions the Company for an expanded 2027 program if results warrant — and the operational commitment of two concurrent rigs signals management's confidence in the system.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $89.50 AS KAZATOMPROM CUTS 8M LBS AND CAMECO TRIMS GUIDANCE — Sprott: 'Investors Act With Conviction'; Term Prices At $91.50 Signal Structural Supply Deficit
snippet: Uranium spot prices held at US$89.50 per pound as of September 2, 2026 — up 16.84% year-over-year — as supply-side cuts from two of the world's largest producers tightened the fundamental outlook: Kazatomprom reduced its 100% production reference level by approximately 8 million pounds to roughly 77 million pounds annually, reserving the option to downflex production by a further 20%, while Cameco cut McArthur River guidance for the second consecutive year. Sprott Asset Management's September uranium market commentary notes that fresh institutional capital is flowing into uranium equities and physical uranium trusts, characterising the September bid as investors 'acting with conviction' following a quiet Q2. Long-term contract prices at US$91.50 per pound — with utilities locking in forward supply at premium to spot — confirms the physical market is pricing in a structural multi-year deficit. The World Nuclear Association forecasts global reactor requirements more than doubling by 2040, driven by SMR deployment and new entrants including AI data centres committing to nuclear power.

headline: FT: GOLD'S RUN ISN'T DONE — Break Above $4,500 Ends Correction From $5,420 Record; $4,300 Is The Bull Market's Pivotal Support Line Ahead Of NFP
snippet: A Financial Times analysis republished on GoldSeek argues that gold's correction from its January 2026 record of $5,420 per ounce is an orderly technical pullback from overbought conditions, not a structural reversal — the metal remains positioned for a breakout above $4,500 that would signal the resumption of the multi-year bull market. The analysis identifies $4,300 as the pivotal support level ahead of Friday's non-farm payrolls report: a hold above that line on a strong jobs print would confirm that September Fed rate-hike expectations are already priced in, while a soft number would collapse the 62–66% hike odds currently priced by futures markets and trigger a fast 5–10% rally. The FT's structural bull case rests on central bank accumulation running at multi-decade highs, G7 sovereign debt monetisation, and six consecutive annual silver supply deficits — factors the piece argues are structural and non-cyclical. The piece notes that gold mining equities remain priced at historically compressed multiples relative to their own free cash flow generation at current gold prices, implying the equity re-rating trade still has significant room to run.

headline: GOLD MARKET EYES $1 TRILLION MILESTONE AS MARGINS REACH TECH-COMPARABLE LEVELS — Decade Of Underinvestment Sets Up Extended Supply Constraint Into The 2030s
snippet: A September 3 analysis circulated via GlobeNewswire highlights that gold mining is approaching a structural market capitalisation inflection point: at $4,400+ per ounce, producers operating with all-in sustaining costs below $1,800 per ounce are generating free cash flow margins that compare favourably with the most profitable sectors in global equities, yet gold mining companies trade at a substantial discount to broad-market P/E multiples. The piece points to a decade of exploration underinvestment across 2015-2023 as the source of supply constraints now building in the pipeline: major deposits discovered today require 7-15 years to reach production, and the number of significant new gold discoveries globally fell sharply during the low-price years. The combination of structurally constrained future supply, elevated current prices, and compressed sector valuations represents the setup that junior exploration companies benefit from directly — producers' need to replace depleted reserves drives M&A interest and exploration funding into early-stage projects at a pace not seen since the 2010 supercycle.
